lesson.title: Who may see what
lesson.subtitle: Roles, summaries, small groups, and why numbers aren't anonymous

video.title: Who may see what
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Joseph — computer studies teacher, Kenya (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.visual: Icon cards: A district report; One pupil in 6B; Everyone knew. Dr Farah beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A district report said: in Class Six B, one pupil has a disability and failed maths. There is one pupil with a disability in Six B. Everyone knew who.

scenes.visual: Paper-grey title card: the Darsi mark, the course name and the lesson title with the Data engineering track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark scales in with a small overshoot; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: who may see what, and how to share data without exposing a child.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Class teacher: her class; Head: the whole school; Parents: their own child; District: summaries.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Start with roles. A class teacher sees her own class. The head sees the whole school. Parents see their own child. The district sees summaries. Each role gets only what it needs: that's least privilege.

scenes.visual: Two columns: “Rows” (A child on every line) and “Summaries” (Averages per class; No names).
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Share summaries, not rows, whenever you can. A class average answers the district's question without a single name. But small groups give people away.

scenes.visual: One big value: 5, Fewer than five pupils? Hide the group.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: So hide any group of fewer than five pupils. One pupil with a disability in Six B is not a statistic; it's a person. Report it at school level, or not at all.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Names become numbers; The list brings names back; So can a few facts.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Replacing names with numbers is a start, not the end. It's called pseudonymisation: whoever holds the list of numbers can bring the names back. And a few ordinary facts can do it too.

scenes.visual: Icon cards: Birth date; Sex; Postcode; 87 in 100 identified.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In a well-known study, birth date, sex and postcode alone picked out eighty-seven people in a hundred in the United States. In a school, a class, an age and one detail can be enough.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Quick check! The district asks for this term's maths results. Which is safest to send?

scenes.visual: Icon cards: Class averages; Groups under 5 hidden; Not row by row.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Averages per class, with groups under five hidden. Numbers instead of names still describe each child, and anyone with the list can match them back.

scenes.visual: Code typed out on a card: SELECT class, COUNT(*) AS n, … Caption: Groups of fewer than five never leave the school
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In SQL, GROUP BY makes the averages, and HAVING drops the small groups. One line of HAVING protects every child in a small class.

scenes.visual: Icon cards joined by arrows: Six harmless posts; Together: a child found; Choose who sees each.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, six harmless posts by Lina, fourteen, add up to her school, her route home and when her house is empty. Choose who sees each one. School data works the same way: each column alone is harmless, but together they point at a child.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. We replaced every name with a number before sharing a file. Is the data anonymous now?

scenes.visual: Summary card: Each role: only what it needs; Summaries, not rows; Hide groups under five; Numbers aren't anonymous. Takeaway bar: Share what the reader needs, never who the child is.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: No: it's pseudonymised, and the list or a few facts can bring the child back. Remember: each role sees only what it needs. Share summaries, and hide groups under five. And numbers instead of names are a start, not the end.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: A made-up pupil; One fact at a time; How many until we know?. Dr Farah beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: play “Guess who” with a made-up pupil. Give one fact at a time: her class, her age, her bus stop, her sports team. After how many facts can the class tell who she is?

checkpoints.prompt: The district asks for this term's maths results. Which is safest to send?

options.text: Every pupil's mark, with numbers instead of names
Averages per class, hiding groups under five

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — averages answer the question, and hiding small groups stops anyone picking out a child.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — rows with numbers still describe each child, and the list can bring the names back. Send averages, small groups hidden.

checkpoints.prompt: Every name was replaced with a number before a file was shared. Is the data anonymous now?

options.text: Yes: without names, nobody can tell
No: it's pseudonymised; the list or a few facts can identify a child
Only if the file is a CSV

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — that's pseudonymisation. Whoever holds the list, or a few other facts, can bring the child back.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — numbers instead of names are pseudonymised, not anonymous: the list or a few facts can identify a child.
